cards.text: Friend, meet John the Baptist, the man who's been out by the Jordan baptizing people with water. It's the next day, and John is there again with two of his disciples. Grab your apron, baker, because this is where it all starts.
Then here comes Jesus, just walking by. John sees Him and speaks up.

cards.question: As Jesus walks by, what does John the Baptist say about Him?

answers.text: Look at the Lamb of God
Look at the Lion of Judah
Look at the Son of David

cards.question: When John's two disciples hear him call Jesus the Lamb of God, they stay right where they are with John.

cards.text: So now two guys are walking right behind Jesus, and Jesus turns and sees them following. You KNOW that moment, friend, when somebody turns around and you have to act like you were headed that way anyway.

cards.question: Jesus asks the two followers, "What do you want?" What do they ask Him back?
When the two followers answer Jesus, they call Him ___, which means Teacher.

cards.text: Jesus answers, "Come and see." No address, no directions, no pin dropped in the group chat, just COME.

cards.question: The two followers go and see where Jesus is staying, and they spend that day with Him.

cards.text: It was about the tenth hour. And one of those two followers has a name: Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.

cards.question: After his day with Jesus, who is the first person Andrew goes and finds?
Andrew tells his brother Simon what they've found. What does he say they've found?

cards.text: Messiah, which is translated as Christ. Andrew brings Simon to Jesus, and Jesus looks at him and says, "You are Simon son of John."

cards.question: Jesus tells Simon son of John he will be called by a new name. What is it?

cards.text: Cephas, which is translated as Peter. Friend, it took an ANGEL and a ride out of a junk drawer just for me to keep MY name, and Simon walks up and gets a brand new one in one sentence.
The next day, Jesus decides to set out for Galilee. And He finds a man named Philip.

cards.question: When Jesus finds Philip, what does He tell Philip to do?

cards.text: Philip is from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter, so somebody's hometown group chat is about to get BUSY. Then Philip goes and finds a man named Nathanael.

cards.question: Philip tells Nathanael who they've found. How does Philip describe Jesus?

answers.text: The One Moses and the prophets wrote about
A new teacher who came from Jerusalem
A priest sent from the temple in Jerusalem

cards.text: Then Philip says where He's from: Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph. Nathanael hears the word Nazareth, and I don't think he's sold.

cards.question: When Nathanael hears that Jesus is from Nazareth, what does he ask?

answers.text: Can anything good come from Nazareth
Where in the world is Nazareth

cards.question: Philip answers Nathanael with the same three words Jesus said to the first two followers: Come and ___.

cards.text: No debate, no slideshow, no forty-five minute speech, just come and see. And as Nathanael walks up, Jesus sees him coming and says something about him.

cards.question: What does Jesus say about Nathanael as he walks up?

answers.text: A true Israelite with no deceit in him
A man who knows the Law by heart
A man who has come a long way

cards.text: I bet Nathanael's jaw hits the FLOOR. He asks, "How do You know me?"

cards.question: Jesus tells Nathanael He saw him before Philip ever called him. Where was Nathanael?
After Jesus tells him about the fig tree, what does Nathanael call Jesus?

answers.text: The Son of God and the King of Israel
A prophet even greater than Moses

cards.text: Friend, Nathanael went from doubting to ALL IN faster than my oven preheats. And Jesus says to him, "Do you believe just because I told you I saw you under the fig tree?"

cards.question: Jesus tells Nathanael that the fig tree is the biggest thing he will ever see.

cards.text: Not even close: Jesus says, "You will see greater things than these." Baker, the fig tree was just the TRAILER.

cards.question: Then Jesus says they will all see heaven open. What will they see ascending and descending on the Son of Man?

cards.text: Heaven open, and the angels of God going up and down. And it all started with two guys following Somebody down the road and getting caught when He turned around.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "Come and see.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says John has been out by the Jordan baptizing people with water. That comes from outside the passage (John 1:26, 28), but the card cites only John 1:35 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Jesus first shows up here, and no card says who He is. The usual short introduction, like "God's Son," would give away the answer to stop 2 card 12, where Nathanael calls Him the Son of God. "The Lamb" would give away stop 1 card 3.
findings.question: Does Jesus need a 'who they are' introduction the first time He appears in a passage? If He does, what wording introduces Him without giving away a later choice card?

findings.problem: The last story card adds nothing new. Card 16 already asked about the open heaven and the angels of John 1:51. This card restates that answer and then recaps John 1:37-38 (the two following Jesus and Him turning around). The card cites only John 1:51. The passage has no story group, so the exception for a final 'story isn't over' line doesn't apply.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 7 of the stop's 9 choice cards are multiple choice. There is only 1 true or false card and 1 fill in the blank card.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only one that sounds like Scripture (Moses and the prophets). Both wrong answers are plain job titles with a hometown ('from Jerusalem'). The right answer also changes 'the One the prophets foretold' into 'the prophets wrote about.'

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This joke ('No debate, no slideshow, no forty-five minute speech, just come and see') uses the same three-part 'No X, no Y, no Z, just come' build as stop 1 card 8. Group chats also appear twice (stop 1 card 8, stop 2 card 3). The docs ban formulas for question types and joke quotas, but they don't say whether a joke shape or reference can come back within one walkthrough.
findings.question: Should Papa Dorin avoid using the same joke structure or the same everyday reference (like the group chat) more than once in a single walkthrough, unless it's a deliberate callback?
